name: Mare Crisium
tip: Find the isolated oval sea near the eastern limb. Its foreshortened outline changes slightly with libration.

name: Mare Fecunditatis
tip: Look for the dark plain against brighter highlands. Follow its outline rather than trying to resolve small surface details.

name: Oceanus Procellarum

name: Mare Serenitatis
tip: Trace the rounded basin north of Tranquillitatis. Follow the contrast between its dark interior and bright surrounding highlands.

name: Mare Tranquillitatis
tip: Compare this dark lava plain with rounder Serenitatis to its north. Apollo 11 landed here; its hardware is far too small to see.

name: Plato
tip: Seek the dark oval at the northern edge of Imbrium. Its floor is recognizable; the tiny craterlets require much more magnification.

name: Ptolemaeus
tip: Follow the large crater outline in the central southern highlands near the terminator; compare it with Alphonsus and Arzachel below.

name: Tycho
tip: Follow the long pale rays across the southern highlands near full Moon. The ray system is much easier than details inside this small crater.

name: Walther
tip: Look for the crater outline close to the light–shadow boundary. Brace or mount your binoculars; interior detail may require a telescope.

name: Aristarchus
tip: Find an unusually bright patch in the western maria. The crater and nearby plateau blend together at low magnification.

name: Grimaldi
tip: Look for the dark, foreshortened oval near the western limb. A steady support helps separate it from surrounding highlands.

name: Kepler
tip: Find the small bright patch west of Copernicus. Its ray halo is easier to recognize than the crater itself in ordinary binoculars.
